summary: Elevated 5xx error floor observed during model stage swap (inflight preemption) for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer GlyphHealth reported a persistent elevated 5xx error floor (primarily 502/503) starting 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC coincident with an orchestrated model stage swap (blue->green) for gptx-13b-v1 variants on their dedicated pool. Errors persisted ~45 minutes with degraded success rate (~87% -> 65%) before mitigation.

Impact:
- Affected live inference requests for GlyphHealth production traffic in us-west-2.
- Observed streaming disconnects for ~3% of sessions and increased tail latency for many in-flight calls.
- Customer reported timeouts surfaced in their logs and elevated error pages in their app.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool for GlyphHealth (reserved capacity).
- Hosts: pool-glyph-prod-usw2-*, model nodes running kernel v2.14.
- Config: autoscaler enabled, prefetch enabled, model pin to gptx-13b-v1 (canary stage swap to quant variant).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Initiate model stage swap via console API to roll traffic from blue->green (2026-03-10 02:38 UTC).
2) Orchestrator scheduled parallel reloads across nodes; a subset of nodes started terminating active model workers and launching replacements.
3) During worker handoff many in-flight requests were preempted and retried, triggering higher upstream load and amplifier retries at the API gateway.
4) API gateway returned a sustained elevation of 502/503 responses while runtime restarted and recovered.

Observed logs / metrics / links:
- Grafana (request success rate): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/somepanel/glyph-prod?from=1646998800000&to=1647001200000
- APIGW error rate spike (502/503) correlating with model-reload events: request_id samples attached in comments.
- Runtime logs show repeated "worker preempted - inflight requests aborted" messages and watcher restarts.

Temporary mitigation enacted:
- Support coordinated with Oncall Runtime lead to pause rolling swap and block further parallel worker terminations at 02:55 UTC.
- Increased soft concurrency limits on affected pool to reduce preemption.
- Applied a temporary per-node graceful-drain timeout increase to allow in-flight KV cache flush (rolled at 03:05 UTC).

Customer impact mitigation status:
- After changes, success rate recovered to ~95% by 03:20 UTC. GlyphHealth enabled degraded-mode retry logic at 03:25 UTC as a safety net.

Requested next steps:
- Root cause investigation into orchestration behavior during stage swap with inflight request preemption.
- Consider a staged, node-by-node swap (no parallel replacements) or increase default graceful-drain window for dedicated pools.
- Investigation into possible APIGW retry amplification during simultaneous worker restarts.
comments: 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC - Jordan Kim (Assignee): Acknowledged. Paused ongoing swap and coordinated with runtime oncall. Collecting runtime logs and request traces. Notified #support and #runtime-oncall.

2026-03-10 03:10 UTC - Aisha Duarte (Runtime Oncall): Found repeated 'kill -9' style preemption on 3 nodes; workers didn't finish KV flush before restart. Linking logs: https://logs.redwood.com/glyph/prod/2026-03-10/0430
2026-03-10 03:22 UTC - Priya Nair (Reporter): Customer confirmed partial recovery but asked for explanation and mitigation plan; they want guarantees to avoid regressions during future swaps.

2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - SRE Lead, Mateo Ruiz: Initial hypothesis: orchestrator allowed parallel replacements beyond safe concurrency for this pool due to aggressive rollout flag. Filed internal ticket INT-19004 to audit rollout config defaults.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Parallel model worker replacement across many nodes caused mass preemption of inflight requests, which amplified retries at API gateway and overran available warm workers.
Hypothesis 2: Graceful-drain timeout is too short for quantized models that require longer KV cache flush; preemption aborted critical cache writes leading to odd runtime restarts.
Evidence: Runtime logs show 'inflight aborted' followed by 'kvcache-warmup failed' on nodes id: pool-glyph-prod-usw2-08, -12, -19. See trace bundle: https://trace.redwood.com/bundle/428307
Related config: autoscaler surge policy allowed up to 4 concurrent replacements per shard during stage swap (default). Consider reducing to 1 for dedicated pools with large model footprints.
Linked internal audit: INT-19004 (rollout-config-audit) may contain reproducer from staging.
resolution:
Workaround and short-term fix: Paused staged swaps for GlyphHealth and increased graceful drain to 90s for dedicated pools with gptx-13b family. We performed a targeted staged rollback and re-applied swap in single-node rolling fashion.

Planned long-term actions:
- Change default stage-swap rollout policy for dedicated pools to single-node rolling by default (RFC in progress).
- Add pre-swap check for inflight request volume and automatic deferral if > threshold.
- Improve APIGW retry logic to avoid amplification when upstream returns transient 5xx during controlled restarts.

Status: Mitigations applied and customer recovery confirmed. Action items assigned to Runtime (Jordan Kim) and Orchestrator (Mateo Ruiz) with target RFC draft by 2026-03-20.
